deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.27): X is a space or topos with a closed 'stratum' Y and open complement X* = X \ Y. On the previous page Grothendieck took, provisionally, V_{Y,X} to be the germ of X around Y. He means it as a topos, namely the projective limit of the open neighbourhoods of Y. He factored Y -> X as Y -> V_{Y,X} -> X, where the first map behaves like a closed immersion and is expected to be a homotopy equivalence, and the second behaves like an open immersion. The motivating case is the one where Y and X* are manifolds but X is singular along Y. The goal is to rebuild X from these 'elementary building pieces'.

On this page he introduces (5) V*_{Y,X} := V_{Y,X} ∩ X* = V_{Y,X} \ Y. This is the germ of punctured neighbourhoods of Y, a deleted tubular neighbourhood. In modern terms it is the (pro-)homotopy link of Y in X. Its homotopy type should be that of the link bundle over Y.

He forms the cartesian square (6): V*_{Y,X} -> V_{Y,X} on top, X* -> X on the bottom, with vertical maps V* -> X* and V -> X. He labels the top arrow 'bouchage des trous le long de Y', i.e. filling in the holes along Y.

He then proposes to regard X as obtained by gluing V_{Y,X} and X* along their intersection V*_{Y,X}. He stresses that this is independent of any local-triviality or smoothness hypothesis. Technically, X is the amalgamated sum, i.e. the pushout or inductive limit in spaces or topoi, of the span (7): X* <- V*_{Y,X} ↪ V_{Y,X}.

For sheaves this is a correct descent statement up to the pro/ind bookkeeping. A sheaf on X amounts to three pieces of data: a sheaf on X*, a sheaf on some neighbourhood U of Y, and an isomorphism on U \ Y, all up to shrinking U. So Sh(X) is the 2-fibre product of Sh(X*) and Sh(germ) over Sh(punctured germ), which means X is the pushout in topoi.

The purpose, made explicit on the next page, is to compute the homotopy type of X as a homotopy pushout of the types of the three pieces, two of them 'infinitesimal'. The first test case is a van Kampen theorem for fundamental groupoids, with π1 V ≅ π1 Y. This is the standard 'link + strata' dévissage of a stratified space, the programme of the 'topos stratifié' notes and of §5 of the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical error on this page.

Gap: V_{Y,X} is a pro-object (a limit of neighbourhoods), not an open subspace. So 'X = V ∪ X*' and the pushout (7) only make sense in a suitable 2-category of topoi or pro-spaces, or after choosing a cofinal neighbourhood.
Gap: the homotopy-pushout statement needs tameness ('modération') hypotheses. Grothendieck acknowledges this on the adjacent pages; at the topos level the gluing itself is fine without them.

ideas.what: Germ of punctured neighbourhoods V*_{Y,X} = V_{Y,X} \ Y as the 'link' object of a stratum
ideas.modern_name: homotopy link / deleted tubular neighbourhood; topos-theoretic analogue: Deligne's oriented product (vanishing topos) Y ×_X X*

ideas.modern_name: homotopy pushout decomposition of a stratified space; gluing/recollement of topoi

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard and correct set-up: punctured-germ link plus pushout decomposition of a space stratified by one closed stratum. It matches ideas already sketched in the Esquisse and is well developed later (Quinn's homotopy links, exit-path and oriented-topos approaches). Nothing here is new to a specialist.
